description: JD.com announced its entry into food delivery, recruiting restaurants with zero commission for a year for merchants signing up before 1 May 2025. Start of the subsidy war.

event_name: First SAMR summons of food-delivery platforms
description: SAMR and four other agencies summoned JD.com, Meituan and Ele.me over competition problems in food delivery, requiring lawful operation and protection of consumers, merchants and riders.
source: SAMR official notice; 13 May 2025 (reported by Caixin and Xinhua)

description: SAMR summoned Ele.me, Meituan and JD.com again, demanding strict compliance, regulated promotional activity and rational competition, after Taobao Instant Commerce announced a RMB 50bn subsidy programme on 2 Jul 2025.

event_name: Platforms pledge to curb irrational subsidies
description: Meituan, Taobao Instant Commerce / Ele.me and JD.com each issued statements pledging to regulate promotions, resist below-cost and disorderly competition, and end practices such as 0-yuan purchases.

event_name: Anti-monopoly committee opens food-delivery competition investigation
description: SAMR disclosed that the Office of the State Council Anti-Monopoly and Anti-Unfair Competition Committee had opened an investigation and assessment of competitive conditions in the food-delivery platform industry.

event_name: SAMR summons seven platforms on involution-style competition
description: SAMR summoned Alibaba, Tencent, Douyin, Baidu, JD.com, Meituan and Taobao Shangou, warning against cutthroat competition and aggressive promotional tactics.

SAMR fined and confiscated a combined RMB 3.597 billion from seven platforms (Pinduoduo, Meituan, JD.com, Ele.me, Douyin, Taobao, Tmall) for failing to vet food vendors (ghost shops), the largest penalty in Food Safety Law history. A food-safety case, but widely read as part of the anti-involution campaign.
source: Reuters; 17 Apr 2026; SAMR English release; 23 Apr 2026

description: SAMR published the draft Ten Provisions on Regulating Subsidy Behaviour of Food Delivery Platforms for public comment (17 Jun to 17 Jul 2026): banning long-term large-scale subsidies that restrict competition, forced merchant participation, and below-cost selling, and requiring advance disclosure of campaigns.
source: SAMR draft via People's Daily / China News Service; 17 Jun 2026 (SCMP; J.P. Morgan research note 18 Jun 2026)

description: At a State Council Information Office press conference for the 15th Five-Year Plan, SAMR pledged coordinated combination-punch measures against involution-style competition, stronger platform oversight of data, algorithms and traffic, and a shift from price competition to quality competition.
source: The Paper / CCTV via press reporting; 20 Sep 2026
